title: Test strategy document
acceptance: tests/STRATEGY.md has sections: test pyramid (unit per module, integration per bounded context, security suite, e2e scenarios per LOB), synthetic-data rule, REQ-xx acceptance mapping, CI reporting to org/quality.json, defect classification and escape tracking
Defect escape section names review.escapedDefects on the originating ticket with a worked example and severity classes
Pyramid references real paths (tests/unit, tests/e2e, tests/synthetic) and the exact node --test command
Mentions only fictional data and no secrets
brief: Write tests/STRATEGY.md (Markdown only, ~2-3 pages). Read org/playbooks/standards.md, product/requirements.md (REQ-xx ids), architecture/contracts/modules.md and org/decisions/*.md first; do not restate ADRs, link them. Sections: 1) Pyramid with layer, owner, location, runner (node --test --disable-warning=ExperimentalWarning), expected ratio and gate: unit per module (tests/unit/<module>), integration per bounded context (module pairs over ctx.forTenant), security suite (tenant isolation, authz, PII redaction, injection on API inputs), e2e scenarios per LOB (tests/e2e, scenarios from tests/synthetic SCENARIOS: auto, home, commercial auto). 2) Synthetic-data rule: only generated, seeded, fictional data; no real carriers/people/logos; VINs valid check digit; how to use generatePolicies/generateScenario deterministically. 3) Acceptance against REQ-xx: table template mapping REQ id -> test file -> status; every story acceptance cites a REQ. 4) CI reporting: how a CI run writes pass/fail/todo counts per layer into org/quality.json (propose the JSON shape; check org/ for existing quality.json or scorecards and stay compatible, do not write the file yourself). t.todo semantics for missing modules. 5) Defect classification: severity S1-S4, type (functional, contract, security, data, perf), found-in phase; escape = defect found after ticket accepted, recorded as review.escapedDefects entry on the originating ticket, plus escape rate metric and the rule that every escape gets a regression test. Keep it concrete and checkable; do not write code.

verdicts.reason: All five sections plus worked review.escapedDefects example present, real paths and node --test command cited, fictional data only; nits for follow-up: generatePolicies/generateScenario signatures and LOB/scenario names and todo statuses for tests/security and tests/e2e now stale vs tests/synthetic and tests/security that exist
